_what: Deterministic grading keys for the stage-3a recognition probe (OPEN item 3). Fixed BEFORE any call is made; taken verbatim from each dataset's own README citation block in /workspace/datasets/<name>/README.md, never from the brief.
_two_lists_and_why: Assembling the payloads exposed something the probe design had missed: SOME identifiers are forced by the task's own content and cannot be redacted without changing the task. voelkel2024's outcome battery IS the paper's title ('antidemocratic attitudes', 'partisan animosity'), so a predictor that echoes those words has told us nothing about recall. Two adapter sample_descriptions DID name their study gratuitously ('Strengthening Democracy Challenge', 'BB-PRIME') and were redacted in this session - a mechanical deletion of a proper noun, not a rewrite of a stimulus. `identity_keys` must therefore be ABSENT from every assembled payload (tools/practice.py asserts this and aborts if not); `content_keys` are expected to be present and are reported, never graded.
_grade: RECOGNISED = an identity_key matched the completion, OR the model's own RESULTS_KNOWN field is YES. UNRECOGNISED = neither. content_keys matched are recorded separately. Both the regex verdict and the self-report are stored so a disagreement is visible rather than resolved.

voelkel2026.recall_window_note: published 2026 - inside any plausible training window, and the closest of the five to the target's construct; the strongest recall risk

vlasceanu2024.recall_window_note: published 2024; a climate tournament but with no trust outcome - a middling recall control

bbprime2025.recall_window_note: published 2025 - inside the window; 'BB-PRIME' was redacted from the adapter's sample_description in this session

voelkel2024.recall_window_note: published 2024, a DEMOCRACY megastudy - the cleanest recall control because nothing about it is climate-trust-adjacent (AGENTS.md / OPEN item 3). But its OUTCOME NAMES are the paper's title, so only identity_keys can be graded here

tappin2023.recall_window_note: published 2023 - inside any plausible training window. Its 24 policy items are a widely used bank, so item recognition is likely and study recognition is the thing being graded.

hackenburg2025.recall_window_note: published 2025 (preprint 2024) - inside the window, and the design (24 LLMs x 3 prompts x 10 issues) is distinctive, so recognition is likely; the probe grades it and the scoreboard row records it

identity_keys: political ideology and trust in scientists
gligoric2025.recall_window_note: published 2025 (Registered Report) - inside the window, and the recall risk is HIGHER than for any other task here: this paper's null IS standing finding 5, so the harness's own prior about message-to-trust effects comes from the study being predicted. TASK_12 pre-registers the consequence: a RECOGNISED verdict quarantines the task instead of scoring it.

identity_keys: effect of seeing scientists as intellectually humble
koetke2024.recall_window_note: published in Nature Human Behaviour in November 2024 - inside any plausible training window, and the second-highest recall risk on the board after gligoric2025: the trust-up / belief-down dissociation is the paper's headline and a model that recalls it would score the ranking rows by memory. TASK_13 pre-registers the consequence: a RECOGNISED verdict quarantines the task instead of scoring it (runs/_trusttask2/PREREG.md).

altenmueller2024.recall_window_note: published in Science Communication in January 2024 - inside any plausible training window. The paper's headline is a CROSSOVER INTERACTION with respondent ideology, not the marginal contrast this task scores, so a recalling model would gain less here than on koetke2024 - but the moralTrust-not-expertise dissociation IS the paper's Study 4b result and would be recalled with it. runs/_trusttask3/PREREG.md pre-registers the same quarantine rule: a RECOGNISED verdict makes the row NOT A SCORE.

orchinik2024.recall_window_note: published in PNAS Nexus in 2024 - inside any plausible training window. The paper's headline is the CONDITIONAL-BELIEF gradient (higher stated consensus -> more perceived bias, a herding inference), not the two passages' marginal ATEs, which the paper reports as small; a recalling model would gain less on the cells this task scores than on koetke2024 or gligoric2025. runs/_trusttask4/PREREG.md pre-registers the same quarantine rule: a RECOGNISED verdict, by regex or by the model's own RESULTS_KNOWN, makes that line's row NOT A SCORE.

kim2024.recall_window_note: Harvard Dataverse 2024, paper widely circulated - inside any plausible training window. Its headline is that CAUSAL evidence beats CONSENSUS messaging on belief while neither moves policy, which is close to what this task scores, so a recalling model gains here. runs/_trusttask5/PREREG.md section 4 pre-registers the quarantine rule.

identity_keys: out of the labs and into the streets
dablander2025.recall_window_note: Registered Report published April 2025 - at the edge of a plausible training window. Its headline IS a null on scientist credibility, which is exactly what a recalling model reproduces for free (finding 77), so the quarantine rule matters more here than usual. `Alex Fraser` and `Rochester University` are IN THE STIMULUS and cannot be removed without changing the task, so per finding 22 they are content_keys - reported, never graded - and not identity keys.

kerwer2025.recall_window_note: PsychArchives deposit 2024-03, ZfP 2025 article; German-language leibniz-institute study on plain-language summaries of meta-analyses. Plausibly inside a 2025-26 training window but low-profile; added 2026-08-25 as an idea_01-held-out study (never practiced, never in any calibration fit).

beall2017.recall_window_note: PLOS ONE 2017 with a 2019 correction; well-cited (Kotcher/Maibach group). Inside any plausible training window. Added 2026-08-25 as an idea_01-held-out study (never practiced, never in any calibration fit).
